name: Proud Presenter
layout: Someone proudly presents an achievement in the caption; the picture behind them shows the disaster it caused.

name: Fixed It Dialogue
layout: 3-4 panels: problem raised, "Done.", "How?", the absurd method. Punchline is the last short line.

name: Expectation vs Reality
layout: 2 panels: the brochure, plan or promise; then the same thing in real life.

name: Job Ad vs The Job
layout: 2 panels: the job advert line over a glossy scene; the actual first day over the real scene.

name: How It Started / How It's Going
layout: 2 panels, same place and people: the hopeful start, then the same scene months later.

name: Day 1 vs Day 400
layout: 2 panels: the same employee on day 1 and on day 400; lines are what they say to a newcomer.

name: Escalation Ladder
layout: 3-4 panels: management's 'solutions' to one problem, each more absurd than the last.

name: Handover Note
layout: Caption is the note left for the next shift; the picture shows what the next shift actually finds.

name: Official Notice
layout: Caption is a real-sounding policy or sign; the picture shows staff following it literally, with absurd results.

name: Two Sides of the Counter
layout: 2 panels of the same moment: what the customer sees, then what is happening behind the counter.

name: Nobody / Management
layout: 2 panels: "Nobody:" over a calm scene; then the manager doing the unrequested, absurd thing.

name: POV
layout: Caption starts with "POV:" and puts the reader in the worker's shoes; the picture is that first-person view.

name: Silent Reaction
layout: 2-3 panels of setup; the last panel is only a face (line is "...") that lands the joke.

name: Meeting Agenda
layout: 3-4 panels, each one agenda item read aloud; the last item reveals the absurd priority.

name: Five Stages
layout: 4 panels: one worker's denial, anger, bargaining and 'acceptance' of a new policy; acceptance is absurd.

name: Training Video vs Shift
layout: 2 panels: the cheerful training video's line; the real shift doing the same task.

name: Boss Quote, Staff Face
layout: Caption is a short quote from the boss; the picture is only the staff's reaction, which is the punchline.

name: Tiny Detail
layout: An ordinary, calm work scene; one small detail in the picture is the joke, and the caption points at it innocently.

name: Outsider Solves It
layout: 2-3 panels: experts stuck on a problem; a customer, child or cleaner solves it in one line.

name: Clock Time-Lapse
layout: 3-4 panels labeled by time (9:00, 9:05, 9:06): a calm start that collapses fast.

name: Ticket Status
layout: Caption is an official status update ("Resolved", "On schedule"); the picture shows the reality.

name: Customer Review
layout: Caption is a cheerful 5-star review; the picture reveals what the customer did not notice.

name: What People Think vs Reality
layout: 2-4 panels: how outsiders (friends, family, the public) imagine this job, line by line, then the reality that wrecks each part. (User idea: a teacher is imagined with quiet, clever students, easy lessons and short hours; the reality is 30 wild kids every hour.)

name: Outsmarted
layout: 2 panels: a worker's confident plan to beat an animal, customer or machine; the other side wins effortlessly. (Invented by the writer in round 5, rated 5.)

name: Specialist Vision
layout: 2 panels: what a normal person sees in a place; what someone from this profession sees in the same place.

name: Distracted Boyfriend
layout: Template: a man turns from his partner (the old duty) toward a passer-by (the shiny new thing).

name: Two Buttons
layout: Template: a sweating person chooses between two buttons; both choices are bad, or the wrong one wins.

name: Drake
layout: Template: rejecting the sensible option (top), approving the absurd one (bottom).

name: Crying Cat Interview
layout: Template: an outsider reads a bad sign as a great sign.

name: Roll Safe
layout: Template: a person taps their temple; the caption is a 'clever' idea that defeats the purpose.

name: This Is Fine
layout: Template: a calm figure with coffee in a room on fire, saying everything is fine.

name: Grave Selfie
layout: Template: a smiling person poses at the grave of something staff lost.

name: Moe Throws Barney Out
layout: Template: a problem is thrown out, then is back at the bar in the next frame.

name: Baboon and Sleeping Lion
layout: Template: someone creeps up on a calm, sleeping target, holding the thing that will wreck it.

name: Fish Bait
layout: Template: a fish bites the same labeled bait again.

name: Soldier Shields the Wrong Side
layout: Template: a soldier heroically shields one side while the attack comes from the other.

name: The Plan
layout: Template: four whiteboard steps of a plan; in step 4 the presenter realizes the plan backfires on them.

name: Expanding Brain
layout: Template: 3-4 rising levels of 'enlightenment', each idea worse than the last.

name: Bike Fall
layout: Template: a cyclist jams a stick into their own wheel, then blames something else on the ground.

name: Is This a Pigeon
layout: Template: someone confidently mislabels an obvious thing.

name: Monkey Looks Away
layout: Template: an awkward glance away when someone asks the uncomfortable question.

name: Clown Makeup
layout: Template: 4 steps of believing the same promise again, ending in full clown makeup.

name: Then vs Now
layout: Template: a strong, capable 'then' beside a feeble 'now', about the same job or team.

name: Trade Offer
layout: Template: 'I receive: ... You receive: ...' with a lopsided deal from management.

name: Desk Relay
layout: 3 panels: one form passes from desk to desk, gathering stamps while the person carrying it visibly ages; at the last desk it is rejected and sent back to the start.

name: Why This Rule Exists
layout: 2 panels: an oddly specific rule, read out as if it's normal; then a flashback to the one ridiculous incident that caused it.

name: Audit Day
layout: 3 panels: the usual chaos; the same place spotless and staged during the one-hour audit visit; the chaos rushing back as the auditor's car leaves.

name: Calm Voice, Chaos Room
layout: 2 panels: the worker's calm, professional line on the phone or radio; then a wide shot of the disaster happening around them during that call.

name: Quiet Shift
layout: 2 panels: the outgoing worker says "Quiet shift, nothing to report!" while already halfway out the door; the incoming worker turns around and sees the aftermath.

name: Back From Vacation
layout: 2 panels: before leaving, "Everything is documented, you'll be fine"; one week later, the return to a scene that shows nobody read it.

name: The Question Nobody Asks
layout: 2-3 panels: a new hire innocently asks why something is done this absurd way; every veteran freezes and turns slowly; the oldest one answers with one quiet line.

name: Just As You Finish
layout: 2 panels: the worker finishes the last task of a long day and relaxes; the exact same second, a huge new job arrives.

name: Load-Bearing Workaround
layout: The picture shows an elaborate improvised fix (tape, buckets, a chair, string) keeping something vital running; the caption calls it by its official system name.

name: Paperwork Scale
layout: 2 panels: a tiny, simple request; then the towering, absurd amount of paperwork and steps needed to do it, shown to scale.

name: Helpful Manager
layout: 3 panels: the team handles a busy moment smoothly; the manager arrives saying "I'm here to help!"; the final panel shows what the help did.

name: Nature Documentary
layout: The caption is a calm wildlife-narrator line describing workers as a species in their habitat; the picture shows the behavior like a nature photo.

name: Live Commentary
layout: 2-3 panels: a dull routine work task described by an over-excited sports commentator, building to a dramatic 'goal' that is something tiny.

name: Movie Trailer
layout: 3-4 panels with dramatic trailer narration ("In a world where...") over ordinary work scenes, ending on the absurd 'title' moment.

name: Scariest Sound
layout: Caption: "The most terrifying sound in this job:"; the picture shows the source of the sound and the workers' horrified faces.

name: Museum Placard
layout: The caption is a museum label for an ancient piece of equipment ("Circa 1990. Still in daily use."); the picture shows it in a glass case while a worker reaches in to use it.

name: Shift Forecast
layout: The caption is a weather forecast for today's shift ("90% chance of..."); the picture shows the forecast already coming true.

name: Recipe for Disaster
layout: 3-4 panels: the 'ingredients' of a typical bad day added one by one, as in a cooking show; the last panel is the finished dish.

name: Group Chat
layout: 3 panels: messages in the team group chat as lines; each picture shows the person sending it and what is really happening where they are.

name: Origin Story
layout: 3 panels: an ordinary new worker; years of one specific torment; the 'superpower' it gave them, shown as a heroic pose.

name: Survival Tip
layout: The caption is a numbered survival tip for the job, said deadpan; the picture shows the tip in action.

name: If It Were Honest
layout: The caption is what an official sign, title or policy would say if it were honest; the picture shows the place it describes.

name: Starter Pack
layout: 3-4 panels, each one object every worker in this job knows; the last object is the punchline.

name: Zoom Out
layout: 2 panels: a close-up that looks fine, even impressive; then the camera pulls back to reveal the absurd context.

name: Dream vs Wake Up
layout: 2 panels: the worker asleep, dreaming of a small, reasonable thing (a full team, a working machine); then waking to the real shift.

name: Kid's Version
layout: 2 panels: a child explains a parent's job in one line over a crayon-style drawing; then the real job, which matches the kid's version uncomfortably well.

name: Unboxing
layout: 3 panels: the exciting arrival of long-requested new equipment; opening the box; what is actually inside.

name: Award Ceremony
layout: The caption names an official award ("Employee of the Month for..."); the picture shows the absurd reason the winner earned it.

name: Standing Ovation
layout: The whole team cheers and applauds wildly; the caption reveals the tiny, basic thing that finally worked.

name: Exit Interview
layout: 2-3 panels of exit-interview questions and answers; the last answer is a short, devastating truth.

name: Performance Review
layout: 2 panels: the manager reads one metric from the review; the picture shows what the worker actually did that day.

name: Team Photo
layout: 2 panels: the cheerful official team photo; the same pose today with only one exhausted person left, holding everyone's tasks.

name: Four Seasons
layout: 4 panels: the same person at the same counter or desk through spring, summer, autumn and winter, still waiting for the same thing.

name: Panik Kalm Panik
layout: Template: 3 faces: panic at a problem, calm at a reassuring detail, panic again at the twist that ruins the reassurance.

name: Always Has Been
layout: Template: astronaut 1 realizes "Wait, it's all X?", astronaut 2 behind him: "Always has been."

name: Pointing at Each Other
layout: Template: two identical figures pointing at each other, each blaming the other for the same problem.

name: Draw 25
layout: Template: a card says "Do the obvious sensible thing or draw 25"; the person is holding a giant stack of 25 cards.

name: Yelling at the Cat
layout: Template: an upset person yells across the table; an unbothered cat at a dinner plate gives a calm, absurd reply.

name: Pained Smile
layout: Template: an older person smiles politely at the camera while their eyes show deep pain.

name: Two Sides of the Bus
layout: Template: two people on a bus; one window shows a sunny view (the optimist), the other a rock wall (the veteran).

name: Swerve to the Exit
layout: Template: a car swerves off the highway (the sensible option) onto the exit ramp (the absurd one).

name: Unmasking
layout: Template: heroes pull the mask off the villain, revealing the real culprit was something unexpected all along.

name: Waiting Skeleton
layout: Template: a skeleton still sitting on a bench, waiting for something management promised.

name: Slaps Roof
layout: Template: a salesman slaps the roof: "This bad boy can fit so much..." about something overloaded.

name: Same Picture
layout: Template: someone is shown two supposedly different things and says, "They're the same picture."

name: Hard Pills
layout: Template: a hand holds a bottle of hard-to-swallow pills; the pill is an uncomfortable truth about the job.

name: Window Envy
layout: Template: a gloomy worker inside looks out the window at others having fun, getting the thing they never get.

name: Shocked Face
layout: Template: someone does the obvious bad thing, then makes a shocked face at the obvious result.

name: Domino Effect
layout: Template: a tiny domino (a small decision) about to topple a giant domino (the disaster).

name: Iceberg
layout: Template: the small visible tip (what management sees) and the huge underwater part (what the work really is).

name: Ant Carries the Elephant
layout: Composition: a tiny, straining ant carries a huge elephant on its back, and the elephant proudly carries one tiny, weightless thing. Labels: the ant is who does the real work; the elephant is who or what gets the credit while doing something trivial; the tiny thing is that trivial task. (User idea.)

name: Fancy Version
layout: Template: a character in plain clothes (the plain name), then in a tuxedo (the fancy corporate name for the same thing).
